title: Why Cats Purr
topic: วิทยาศาสตร์
lines: Most people think cats purr only when they are happy. It is true that a
cat often purrs while it is being stroked, but **this** is not the whole
story. Cats also purr when they are hungry, frightened or even injured.
Mother cats purr to guide their kittens, which are born blind, and the
kittens purr back to show **they** are safe.
Some scientists believe purring may also help cats heal. The vibrations
of a purr are between 25 and 150 times per second, and sound waves at
**these** levels have been shown to help bones and muscles repair in
humans. This could explain why cats seem to recover from falls and
broken bones faster than dogs. However, more research is needed before
doctors can use purring sounds as medicine. For now, **many** cat owners
simply enjoy the sound. As one owner put it, "When my cat purrs on my lap
after a long day, I feel calmer too. Maybe **it** helps both of us."
